Irene: Published the postmortem for yesterday's rollout variance: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2141597531-rollout-variance
Irene: TL;DR: a subtle timing difference between the rollout orchestrator and the model cache priming caused a small window where nodes returned stale kernels. Result: elevated error-rate and degraded responses for ~27 minutes.
Irene: Full doc has timeline, config diff, repro steps, and anonymized request traces. Read before the sync.
Irene: Action items called out (owners + targets):
- Omar 0 0: make the orchestrator enforce a cache-primed precondition before traffic shift + add unit test harness 0 target 2026-04-06
- Tessa 0: add a guarded rollout flag and a small canary expansion stepper (5% -> 25% -> 100%) 0 target 2026-04-02
- Vik 0: add a dashboard for "stale-kernel-rate" and an alert when >0.1% for 5m 0 target 2026-03-31
Irene: Also added a short customer impact section and a support detection snippet. Please review owners and note any conflicts.
Omar: I'll take the orchestrator change. Planning to include an integration test that simulates simultaneous cache invalidation. Will link PR to doc.
Tessa: I'll prototype the guarded rollout flag this week. Suggest we also include a max-step-duration safety check to avoid rapid expansion during noisy periods.
Vik: I'll add the metric and dashboard; proposing an early-warning tier (info level) at 0.03% before the main alert.
SupportBot: Incident INC-9321 created: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-9321
Irene: Scheduling a 25-min follow-up checkpoint Monday 10:00 PT to review PRs and canary params: https://calendar.internal/meet/rollout-safety
Omar: Can someone paste the spike trace we saw? Want to reproduce exact timing.
Tessa: Pasted the trace in doc and attached the minimal harness to reproduce the timing skew.
Vik: I'll include dashboard mockups in the doc before the meeting.
Irene: Thanks all. If you can't attend, leave a note in the doc with blockers. We'll aim to close actions within two weeks. :thumbsup:
